name: Otaku Culture
description: Questions covering: Anime Studios, Manga Artists, Anime Directors, Vocaloid, Cosplay...

questions.question: Which animation studio produced the Oscar-winning film 'Spirited Away'?
questions.explanation_correct: Founded by Miyazaki and Takahata, Ghibli is famous for its lush hand-drawn animation.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Gainax, Madhouse and Production I.G are other animation studios; Spirited Away was produced by Studio Ghibli.

questions.question: Which manga artist created Astro Boy?
questions.explanation_correct: Osamu Tezuka created Astro Boy and is often called the god of manga. His work helped define modern manga storytelling.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are prominent manga creators, but they are not the creator of Astro Boy. Their major works are different from Tezuka's.

questions.question: Who directed Neon Genesis Evangelion?
questions.explanation_correct: Hideaki Anno directed Neon Genesis Evangelion. He is strongly identified with the series and its later film projects.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are well-known directors, but they did not direct Neon Genesis Evangelion. They are associated with different anime works.

questions.question: Which virtual singer developed by Crypton Future Media is known for long teal twin-tails and the name Miku?
questions.explanation_correct: Hatsune Miku is a virtual singer and character developed by Crypton Future Media, recognizable by her teal twin-tails.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Luka, Rin and Teto are other virtual singer characters.

questions.question: What term refers to costume roleplay fandom activity?
questions.explanation_correct: Cosplay is the practice of wearing costumes and portraying fictional characters. It is a major part of fan culture at conventions and online.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options refer to different fan activities or products. They do not specifically mean dressing as a character.

questions.question: What Japanese term refers to dedicated pop-culture fans?
questions.explanation_correct: Otaku is the Japanese term for people with intense dedication to anime, manga, games, or related interests. Its usage can vary from neutral to critical depending on context.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are Japanese terms, but they refer to different concepts. They do not specifically mean devoted pop-culture fandom.

questions.question: What Japanese term refers to independently published works, including many fan-made comics?
questions.explanation_correct: Dōjinshi are independently published works, often comics; they can be original or based on existing stories.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are other forms of Japanese publishing or comics, but they are not the specific term for self-published fan works. They have broader or different meanings.

questions.question: Which Japanese event at Makuhari Messe in Chiba is particularly known for garage kits and collectible figures?
questions.explanation_correct: Wonder Festival is a major event for figures and garage kits. Its Japanese editions have been held at Makuhari Messe in Chiba.
questions.explanation_incorrect: AnimeJapan, Tokyo Game Show and Jump Festa have different principal focuses.

questions.question: What is the popular nickname for the Comic Market event?
questions.explanation_correct: Comiket is the common nickname for Comic Market, Japan's huge doujin convention. It is one of the largest fan conventions in the world.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are convention-style names, but they are not the standard nickname for Comic Market. They do not refer to the same event.

questions.question: What term describes affectionate appeal toward fictional characters?
questions.explanation_correct: Moe refers to a feeling of affection or protective warmth toward fictional characters. It is a key concept in anime and manga fandom.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other terms are related to anime aesthetics or character types, but they are not the same concept. They describe different aspects of fandom and characterization.

questions.question: What term describes an anime personality type that acts cold at first but becomes affectionate later?
questions.explanation_correct: Tsundere refers to a character who is initially abrasive or distant but gradually shows warmth or affection. It is a common archetype in anime and manga.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options describe different personality archetypes or behaviors. They do not specifically mean cold-then-warm.

questions.question: Which Tokyo district is especially famous for otaku shopping and pop-culture stores?
questions.explanation_correct: Akihabara is a Tokyo neighborhood known for electronics, anime, manga, and otaku-focused shopping. It is a major hub of Japanese pop culture.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other districts are well-known Tokyo areas, but they are not primarily associated with otaku shopping. None matches Akihabara's specific reputation.

questions.question: Which franchise is known for giant robots called mobile suits?
questions.explanation_correct: Gundam is a mecha franchise centered on giant robots called mobile suits. It is one of the most influential series in the genre.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are mecha-related series, but they are not the franchise identified by mobile suits. They refer to different robot settings or titles.

questions.question: Which heroine franchise features Usagi Tsukino as its lead character?
questions.explanation_correct: Usagi Tsukino is the main character of Sailor Moon. The series is one of the most famous magical girl franchises.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are also magical girl or similar series, but they do not center on Usagi Tsukino. They are different franchises entirely.

questions.question: Which Japanese company is best known for producing Nendoroid figures?
questions.explanation_correct: Good Smile Company is widely known for Nendoroid figures. It is a major manufacturer in the anime figure market.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other companies also make figures or collectibles, but they are not the brand most associated with Nendoroids. They produce different lines or products.

questions.question: Which film director is known for directing Spirited Away and My Neighbor Totoro?
questions.explanation_correct: Hayao Miyazaki is the acclaimed director behind films such as Spirited Away and My Neighbor Totoro. He is one of the most famous anime filmmakers.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are prominent directors, but they are not the filmmaker associated with those Studio Ghibli classics. Each has a different body of work.

questions.question: What term refers to the Japanese manga and anime demographic aimed at young boys?
questions.explanation_correct: Shōnen is the demographic label for manga and anime aimed primarily at young male audiences. It is commonly used in publishing classifications.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other terms refer to different audience groups. They do not mean the young boys' demographic.

questions.question: What is the Japanese term for a voice actor or voice actress in anime?
questions.explanation_correct: Seiyuu is the Japanese term used for voice actors in anime, games, and related media. It specifically refers to voice performers.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options describe a manga creator, a fan, or a costume role-player. None of them means voice actor.

questions.question: Which company is known for the Nendoroid line of figures with oversized heads and swappable faceplates?
questions.explanation_correct: The Nendoroid line by Good Smile Company is a staple of modern otaku collecting.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Figma focuses on articulated action figures, and Bandai is known for model kits like Gunpla.

questions.question: Which streaming platform is especially known for anime distribution?
questions.explanation_correct: Crunchyroll is a major streaming service focused on anime distribution. It is one of the best-known anime platforms worldwide.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other services stream many kinds of content, including some anime, but they are not as specifically identified with anime distribution. They are broader entertainment platforms.

questions.question: What is the name of Yamaha’s singing-voice synthesis software?
questions.explanation_correct: Vocaloid is a vocal synthesis software engine developed for creating singing voice tracks. It became widely associated with anime and otaku music culture.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Synthesizer V and CeVIO are other voice-synthesis products; UTAU is a separate singing-synthesis program.

questions.question: What shortened term is commonly used for songs associated with anime?
questions.explanation_correct: Anisong is the common abbreviation for anime songs, especially themes associated with anime. It is widely used in fan and industry contexts.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Seiyuu means voice actor, mangaka means manga artist, and mecha refers to machines or robot-centered fiction.

questions.question: Which Japanese term refers to a female character who wears glasses?
questions.explanation_correct: Meganekko is the archetype term for a girl characterized by wearing glasses. It is a recognizable character type in anime and manga.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options describe different personality or femininity archetypes, not glasses-wearing characters. They are not equivalent to the requested term.

questions.question: Which studio is acclaimed for its high-quality animation in series like 'K-On!' and 'Violet Evergarden'?
questions.explanation_correct: Often called KyoAni, the studio is famous for its attention to detail and employee-centric model.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Madhouse and Bones are known for action-oriented series like Hunter x Hunter or Fullmetal Alchemist.

questions.question: Which Shueisha weekly magazine serialized One Piece, Naruto and Dragon Ball?
questions.explanation_correct: Weekly Shonen Jump serialized all three series and is published by Shueisha.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are different manga magazines.

questions.question: Which Japanese term refers to the robot-anime genre?
questions.explanation_correct: Mecha is the genre term used for works centered on robots or mechanical suits. It is a standard classification in anime and manga.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices refer to different genres or formats, such as fantasy transport, sports, or comedy manga. They are not robot-anime terms.

questions.question: Which Osaka entertainment district is strongly associated with otaku shops and electronics?
questions.explanation_correct: Nipponbashi in Osaka is known for its otaku-related stores, electronics shops, and hobby culture. It is often compared with other major anime retail districts.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other districts are famous Osaka areas, but they are not the specific otaku-centered neighborhood described. They serve different commercial or entertainment roles.

questions.question: What is the Japanese term for visiting real locations that appear in anime or manga?
questions.explanation_correct: Seichi junrei literally means a pilgrimage to sacred or model locations, and fans use it for visiting places depicted in anime or manga. It is a well-established fan practice.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are plausible-sounding phrases, but they are not the established Japanese term for this activity. They do not match the standard usage.

questions.question: Which visual novel developer is known for titles such as Kanon and Clannad?
questions.explanation_correct: Key is the game developer associated with landmark visual novels like Kanon and Clannad. It is one of the most influential names in the genre.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Nitroplus, Type-Moon and 07th Expansion are associated with other visual novels.

questions.question: Which massive fan event takes place annually at the Los Angeles Convention Center?
questions.explanation_correct: AX is the largest anime convention in North America, often debuting major trailers and guests.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Otakon is held on the East Coast, and Comic-Con is primarily in San Diego.

questions.question: In Japanese social and school settings, what term refers to a senior or upperclassman?
questions.explanation_correct: Senpai is the term for a senior, upperclassman, or more experienced member in a hierarchy. It is widely used in anime and related fan contexts.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Kōhai refers to a junior, sensei to a teacher, and otōto to a younger brother. Sempai is an alternative romanization of senpai.

questions.question: Which character archetype describes someone whose extreme, obsessive love leads to violence?
questions.explanation_correct: A yandere is a character archetype defined by an obsessive, intense love that often manifests as violence.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Tsundere, kuudere and deredere describe other personality archetypes.

questions.question: Which character archetype describes someone who is cool, detached, and emotionally restrained?
questions.explanation_correct: A kuudere character is calm, stoic, and emotionally reserved, often showing affection in subtle ways. This archetype is common in anime and manga.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options describe a hot-and-cold personality, an obsessive personality, or an energetic personality.

questions.question: Which Utau voicebank mascot is known for twin drill-shaped hair buns and a gray-blue outfit?
questions.explanation_correct: Kasane Teto is a well-known UTAU voicebank mascot created by fans and later embraced in broader vocal synth culture. She is recognizable for her distinctive twin drill hairstyle.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different vocal synth characters from a separate line or do not match the Utau mascot described.

questions.question: Which anime studio is credited with producing series such as Mobile Suit Gundam?
questions.explanation_correct: Sunrise is an anime studio famous for the Mobile Suit Gundam franchise and many other mecha titles. It has been a major industry name for decades.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are anime studios as well, but they are not the one most directly associated with Gundam.

questions.question: Which shōjo manga magazine published Cardcaptor Sakura and Sailor Moon?
questions.explanation_correct: Kodansha’s Nakayoshi serialized both Cardcaptor Sakura and Sailor Moon.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Ribon, Bessatsu Margaret and LaLa are other shōjo manga magazines.

questions.question: Which visual novel developer is known for Tsukihime and Fate/stay night?
questions.explanation_correct: Type-Moon developed major visual novels including Tsukihime and Fate/stay night. It is also associated with the broader Fate franchise.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are real developers, but they are not the one responsible for those specific titles.

questions.question: Which anime convention moved to the Walter E. Washington Convention Center in Washington, D.C., in 2017?
questions.explanation_correct: Otakon moved to Washington, D.C., in 2017 after many years in Baltimore.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Anime Expo, MomoCon and A-Kon are different conventions.

questions.question: Which figure manufacturer produces the ARTFX line?
questions.explanation_correct: Kotobukiya is a figure and hobby manufacturer known for producing many character figures, including the ArtFX line. It is a staple brand among collectors.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Good Smile Company, Bandai and Alter are other companies in the figure and collectibles market.

questions.question: Which anime streaming service was long associated with licensing and simuldubbing anime for English-speaking audiences?
questions.explanation_correct: Funimation was a major anime streaming and licensing platform, especially known for English dubs and simuldubs. It played a central role in anime distribution for many years.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are streaming platforms too, but they are not the one historically most associated with that role.

questions.question: Which demographic label refers to manga marketed toward adult women?
questions.explanation_correct: Josei is the demographic label used for manga aimed at adult women. It is distinct from shonen, seinen, and kodomo by its intended readership.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different manga demographic labels with different target audiences. Only josei matches adult women.

questions.question: Which Kadokawa light-novel imprint publishes Sword Art Online?
questions.explanation_correct: Sword Art Online by Reki Kawahara is published in Japan under Kadokawa’s Dengeki Bunko imprint.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Fujimi Fantasia Bunko and MF Bunko J are also Kadokawa imprints; GA Bunko is an SB Creative imprint.

questions.question: Which maid café chain styles its name with an @ sign?
questions.explanation_correct: @home cafe is a Japanese maid café chain.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are also maid cafés; the written name identifies @home cafe.

questions.question: Which anime director is known for films such as 'The Girl Who Leapt Through Time' and 'Belle'?
questions.explanation_correct: Mamoru Hosoda directed films including The Girl Who Leapt Through Time and Belle. He is a prominent anime filmmaker known for emotionally driven stories.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other directors are major anime filmmakers, but they did not direct those specific films. Only Mamoru Hosoda fits the clue.

questions.question: Which anime database and tracking site is commonly abbreviated MAL?
questions.explanation_correct: MyAnimeList, often abbreviated MAL, lets users catalog and rate anime and manga.
questions.explanation_incorrect: AniDB, Kitsu and Anime-Planet also catalog anime, but MAL abbreviates MyAnimeList.

questions.question: Which North American distributor released the Lupin the Third: The Castle of Cagliostro anime film on home video?
questions.explanation_correct: Discotek Media has licensed and released The Castle of Cagliostro on home video in North America.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other companies also distribute anime, but Discotek released this film.

questions.question: Which streaming service is associated with Sentai Filmworks anime licenses?
questions.explanation_correct: HIDIVE streams many titles associated with Sentai Filmworks.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Crunchyroll, Netflix and Funimation are other streaming services; Funimation’s service was shut down in 2024.

questions.question: Which company is listed as the manufacturer of the figma Makima figure, distributed by Good Smile Company?
questions.explanation_correct: Good Smile Company lists Max Factory as the manufacturer of figma Makima and itself as distributor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Good Smile Company distributes this figure; Kotobukiya and Alter are other figure companies.

questions.question: Which major hobbyist event is most closely associated with the exhibition and sale of garage kits in Japan?
questions.explanation_correct: Wonder Festival, or WonFes, is a major event featuring figures and garage kits.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Comiket focuses on independently published works, while AnimeJapan and Jump Festa cover broader anime and manga properties.

questions.question: Which company created the Hatsune Miku voicebank and character, initially released for Yamaha’s VOCALOID engine?
questions.explanation_correct: Crypton Future Media created Hatsune Miku; Yamaha developed the VOCALOID synthesis platform.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Yamaha developed the engine, while AHS and Internet Co., Ltd. are associated with other voice products.

questions.question: Which developer studio is associated with visual novels such as Phantom of Inferno and Saya no Uta?
questions.explanation_correct: Nitroplus developed the visual novels Phantom of Inferno and Saya no Uta.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Key, Aqua Plus and 5pb. are other game developers or publishers.

questions.question: Which light-novel imprint originated with Media Factory and is now part of Kadokawa?
questions.explanation_correct: MF Bunko J began as a Media Factory imprint and is now a Kadokawa light-novel label.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Dengeki Bunko and Fantasia Bunko are other Kadokawa labels; GA Bunko is an SB Creative label.

questions.question: What is the manga demographic category for works aimed at adult men?
questions.explanation_correct: Seinen is the demographic label used for manga aimed at adult men. It is different from age- or gender-targeted categories for younger readers or women.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Shōnen targets boys, josei targets adult women, and kodomo targets children, so they do not fit this description.

questions.question: What is the manga demographic category for works aimed at adolescent girls?
questions.explanation_correct: Shōjo is the demographic category for manga aimed at adolescent girls. It is one of the standard manga demographic labels.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Shōnen is for boys, seinen is for adult men, and josei is for adult women, so they are not the correct match.

questions.question: Which event brand was formed by a collaboration between C3 and Anime Festival Asia?
questions.explanation_correct: C3 AFA was announced in 2017 as a collaboration between the organizers of C3 and Anime Festival Asia.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Comiket, Wonder Festival and AnimeJapan are separate events.

questions.question: Which director is known for films such as Perfect Blue and Paprika?
questions.explanation_correct: Satoshi Kon directed acclaimed films including Perfect Blue and Paprika. He is the correct answer to this director clue.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Mamoru Hosoda, Hideaki Anno, and Makoto Shinkai are all notable directors, but they did not direct those films.

questions.question: Which creator is known for works such as Cardcaptor Sakura and XXXHolic?
questions.explanation_correct: CLAMP is a manga creator group responsible for series including Cardcaptor Sakura and XXXHolic. This makes it the correct answer.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Rumiko Takahashi, Naoko Takeuchi, and Ai Yazawa are all manga creators, but they are not the collective behind those works.

questions.question: What is the term for a character archetype marked by over-the-top, self-important imagination?
questions.explanation_correct: Chūnibyō describes a person with an exaggerated, often fantastical sense of self.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Tsundere, yandere, and kuudere are different archetypes defined by emotional behavior, not this style of self-delusion or theatrics.

questions.question: What is the cheer routine term often performed by idol fans at live events?
questions.explanation_correct: Wotagei, also written otagei, refers to coordinated cheering and dance-like movements performed by fans.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Moyashi means bean sprouts; sado refers to the tea ceremony and ikigai to a sense of purpose.

questions.question: Which idol anime franchise features groups such as μ's and Aqours?
questions.explanation_correct: Love Live! is the idol anime franchise associated with groups like μ's and Aqours. It is the correct franchise title for this clue.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Idolmaster, BanG Dream!, and Pretty Rhythm are all idol or music franchises, but they are different series.

questions.question: Which award is given in the annual anime fan poll known for selecting a top title?
questions.explanation_correct: The Anime Grand Prix is an annual award based on a fan poll in anime magazines. It recognizes popular anime titles and related categories.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are awards in different fields or with different selection methods. They are not the specific fan-voted anime poll award.

questions.question: Which Kadokawa anime magazine shares its name with a term from Mobile Suit Gundam?
questions.explanation_correct: Newtype is an anime magazine published by Kadokawa; its title refers to the Gundam term.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Animage is another anime magazine, while Manga Time and Shonen Jump are manga publications.

questions.question: Which term refers to manga or anime aimed at young children?
questions.explanation_correct: Kodomo is the demographic category for children. It is distinct from youth and adult-oriented manga categories.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options refer to other audience groups. They do not denote content specifically for young children.

questions.question: Which descriptive term is used for eyes that slope sharply upward at the outer corners?
questions.explanation_correct: Tsurime describes upward-slanting, sharp-looking eyes in character design. It is a common Japanese face-shape descriptor in anime fandom.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options describe different eye shapes or animal-like archetypes. They are not the term for upward-slanting eyes.

questions.question: Which greeting is commonly used by staff when welcoming a customer back in a maid café?
questions.explanation_correct: Okaerinasai means 'welcome home' and is commonly used in maid cafés. It fits the café roleplay style where customers are treated as returning masters.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other phrases are general greetings or farewells. They are not the customary welcome used in maid cafés.

questions.question: Which major Japanese retail chain is symbolized by its blue and white logo and many tiered specialty floors?
questions.explanation_correct: Animate is Japan's largest retailer for anime, manga, and hobby-related goods.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Book Off focuses on secondhand goods, and Tsutaya is traditionally a media rental shop.

questions.question: Which garage-kit event held an edition in Kobe in October 2013?
questions.explanation_correct: Treasure Festa in Kobe 5 was held at Kobe International Exhibition Hall in October 2013.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Comiket, Jump Festa and AnimeJapan are separate events with different primary focuses.

questions.question: Which term is used in fandom for a woman who enjoys male-male romantic pairings?
questions.explanation_correct: Fujoshi is the term for female fans who enjoy boys' love or male-male pairings. It is a well-known fandom label in otaku culture.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options refer to different fan identities or unrelated terms. They do not specifically denote this fandom category.

questions.question: Which term is used in fandom for a man who enjoys male-male romantic pairings?
questions.explanation_correct: Fudanshi is the term for male fans who enjoy boys' love or male-male pairings. It parallels the more common female-oriented term fujoshi.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Fujoshi is a female fan label, otaku is a broader fan label, and bishōnen describes an attractive young man.

questions.question: Which anime studio is known for producing titles such as Death Note and Perfect Blue?
questions.explanation_correct: Madhouse is a Japanese animation studio known for numerous acclaimed series and films, including Death Note and Perfect Blue. It has a strong reputation for varied, high-quality productions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are also anime studios, but they are not the one associated with those specific titles. They represent different production companies.

questions.question: Which visual novel developer is known for titles such as To Heart and Routes?
questions.explanation_correct: Leaf is a Japanese visual novel developer associated with works like To Heart and Utawarerumono. It fits the developer-name clue in this category.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Key, Nitroplus and Type-Moon are associated with other visual novels.

questions.question: Which franchise centers on managing performers such as Haruka Amami and Miki Hoshii?
questions.explanation_correct: The Idolmaster is the media franchise featuring idol producers and characters like Haruka Amami. It is one of the best-known idol game and anime franchises.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are idol-related franchises, but they are distinct from The Idolmaster. They share the same category without matching the specific target.

questions.question: Which convention held in North Carolina is known for anime, Japanese culture, and cosplay events?
questions.explanation_correct: Animazement is an anime convention held in North Carolina with a focus on anime and Japanese pop culture. It is the target convention name in this clue.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other conventions are real anime events, but they are held in different locations. They fit the same semantic category without being the correct convention.

questions.question: Which shoujo manga magazine first published series such as Sailor Moon and Cardcaptor Sakura?
questions.explanation_correct: Nakayoshi is a shoujo manga magazine historically associated with series like Sailor Moon and Cardcaptor Sakura. It matches the magazine-title clue.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other titles are also manga magazines, but they are not Nakayoshi. They belong to the same category while remaining incorrect.

questions.question: Which brand name is associated with numbered lottery-style prize figures sold through anime merchandise campaigns?
questions.explanation_correct: Ichiban Kuji is a lottery-style merchandise brand whose prizes can include figures and other collectibles.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Banpresto, figma and the fictional Prize-Style are not the lottery brand in the question.

questions.question: Which award and event in Kobe recognized notable anime works and creators?
questions.explanation_correct: Anime Kobe was an anime-related award and event in Kobe that honored works and creators.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are different awards or festivals.

questions.question: Which purple-themed Vocaloid mascot is inspired by the voice of Chihiro Ishiguro?
questions.explanation_correct: Yuzuki Yukari is a Vocaloid character whose voicebank is based on voice actor Chihiro Ishiguro.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Hatsune Miku, Kagamine Rin and Megurine Luka use other voice providers.

questions.question: Which company produced the 1/7-scale Caster/Murasaki Shikibu figure from Fate/Grand Order released in December 2022?
questions.explanation_correct: Alter lists Caster/Murasaki Shikibu as a 1/7-scale Fate/Grand Order figure released in December 2022.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Good Smile Company, Kotobukiya and Max Factory are different figure manufacturers.

questions.question: Which anime studio produced Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood, Mob Psycho 100, and Space Dandy?
questions.explanation_correct: Bones is the anime studio behind series including Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood, Mob Psycho 100, and Space Dandy. It matches the studio-name clue exactly.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are also anime studios, but they did not produce the listed combination. They are in the correct category while remaining incorrect.

questions.question: Which publishing label is responsible for the light novel series 'Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon?' written by Fujino Omori?
questions.explanation_correct: The series is published under SB Creative's 'GA Bunko' imprint.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Dengeki Bunko and Kadokawa Sneaker Bunko are major rival labels but do not publish this specific series.

questions.question: Which Hakusensha shōjo manga magazine serialized Natsuki Takaya’s Fruits Basket?
questions.explanation_correct: Fruits Basket was serialized in Hana to Yume, published by Hakusensha.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Nakayoshi, Margaret and Bessatsu Friend are other shōjo manga magazines.

questions.question: Which streaming service released Cyberpunk: Edgerunners as an anime series in 2022?
questions.explanation_correct: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners was released on Netflix in 2022.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Crunchyroll, Hulu and Amazon Prime Video are separate streaming services.

questions.question: Which phrase is often chanted in maid cafés as a playful “magic spell” over food?
questions.explanation_correct: “Moe moe kyun” is a playful phrase used in maid-café performances, including rituals over food.
questions.explanation_incorrect: “Okaerinasai goshujin-sama” is a welcome-home greeting; “itadakimasu” is said before eating and “konnichiwa” is a general greeting.

questions.question: Which term describes a character who is characterized by high energy and optimism?
questions.explanation_correct: 'Genki' translates to 'healthy' or 'energetic' in Japanese and is a common trope in comedy anime.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Tsundere and kuudere refer to different personality shifts involving coldness or distance.

questions.question: Which convention focuses on Shueisha’s Jump manga properties?
questions.explanation_correct: Jump Festa features manga and anime properties associated with Shueisha’s Jump magazines.
questions.explanation_incorrect: AnimeJapan, Comiket and Niconico Chokaigi are different events.

questions.question: Which 2024 animated film directed by Naoko Yamada explores the emotional experiences of students, focusing on a protagonist who can see colors associated with others' feelings?
questions.explanation_correct: The Colors Within (Kimi no Iro) is a 2024 feature directed by Naoko Yamada about music and a girl who sees people as colors.
questions.explanation_incorrect: While Yamada directed the other films, they were released in previous years.

questions.question: Which visual novel studio created Muv-Luv?
questions.explanation_correct: The visual novel Muv-Luv was developed by âge.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Key, Nitroplus and Lump of Sugar are different visual novel studios.

questions.question: What is a coordinated sequence of fan chants at Japanese idol performances often called?
questions.explanation_correct: A mix is a recognizable sequence of coordinated calls used by idol fans during performances.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Wotagei refers more broadly to fan cheering and dance-like movements; “call” is a more general term.

questions.question: Which eye-type term describes eyes with a downward-slanting impression?
questions.explanation_correct: Tareme describes eyes that appear softly drooping or downward-slanted.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Tsurime describes upturned eyes; sanpaku refers to visible white above or below the iris.

questions.question: What is the common abbreviation for the anime-song concert event Animelo Summer Live?
questions.explanation_correct: Anisama is short for Animelo Summer Live, a major anime-song concert event.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A live house is a music venue, and a one-man live is a concert by a single act.

questions.question: Who wrote the 1983 Manga Burikko column “Otaku Research”?
questions.explanation_correct: Akio Nakamori wrote the 1983 column, an influential early use of otaku as a label for fans.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Katsuhiro Otomo, Osamu Tezuka and Yoshihiro Togashi are manga creators.

questions.question: Which anime database’s name abbreviates “Anime DataBase”?
questions.explanation_correct: AniDB stands for Anime DataBase and catalogs information about anime.
questions.explanation_incorrect: MyAnimeList, Anime News Network and IMDb are other media sites; their names are not abbreviated AniDB.

questions.question: Which famous marketplace is widely associated with digital downloads for doujin games and visual novels?
questions.explanation_correct: DLsite is a major Japanese digital marketplace for doujin works, including visual novels. It is especially well known in otaku circles.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are digital storefronts or platforms, but they are not the one most associated with Japanese doujin and visual novel sales. They serve broader or different publishing ecosystems.

questions.question: Which prize figure brand is a major producer of affordable anime merchandise prizes in arcades?
questions.explanation_correct: Banpresto is famous for prize figures and arcade exclusives in Japan. Its products are a staple of figure collecting culture.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are figure and model manufacturers, but they are not primarily known as prize-figure arcade brands. They target different segments of the hobby.

questions.question: Which Love Live! series centers on the school idol group Aqours?
questions.explanation_correct: Aqours is the school idol group at the center of Love Live! Sunshine!!.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other titles belong to different music or idol franchises.

questions.question: Which Japanese anime-song label releases music for the Love Live! franchise?
questions.explanation_correct: Lantis is a music label associated with anime and game songs, including Love Live! releases.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Avex Trax, King Records and Sony Music are other labels that also release anime-related music.

questions.question: Which magazine is synonymous with 'cute girls doing cute things' 4-panel manga?
questions.explanation_correct: This magazine published the original manga for hits like K-On! and Hidamari Sketch.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Weekly Shonen Jump focuses on action, and Young Magazine targets an older male demographic.

questions.question: Which maid café chain opened its first Akihabara shop in 2008 and describes its setting as a “dream kingdom”?
questions.explanation_correct: Maidreamin opened in Akihabara in 2008 and uses a dream-kingdom theme.
questions.explanation_incorrect: @home cafe, Cure Maid Cafe and Pinafore are other maid cafés.

questions.question: What is the Japanese term for the younger sister character type in anime and manga archetypes?
questions.explanation_correct: Imouto literally means younger sister and is used as a character archetype in otaku media. It refers to a specific sibling role and associated personality conventions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options describe different archetypes or family-role terms. They do not denote the younger sister type requested here.

questions.question: Which shrine is famously linked to Lucky Star pilgrimages and anime tourism?
questions.explanation_correct: Washinomiya Shrine became a well-known pilgrimage site because of its connection to Lucky Star. Fans visit it as part of anime tourism in Japan.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other shrines are real and historically significant, but they are not the one specifically associated with this anime. They are not the famous Lucky Star pilgrimage destination.
